context: Mobile app with varying screen sizes and bandwidth constraints. Multiple client teams (iOS, Android, Web).
expected: REST: simpler caching (HTTP caching, CDN), better tooling, predictable payloads. Wide adoption means easier hiring. GraphQL: clients request exactly what they need, reducing over-fetching on bandwidth-constrained mobile. Single endpoint simplifies versioning. However, complex queries can harm server performance, caching is harder, and the N+1 problem requires careful resolver design.

context: Single-user desktop application with occasional read-heavy queries.
expected: SQLite: zero configuration, no separate server process, ACID compliant, excellent for single-writer workloads. No network overhead. PostgreSQL: richer feature set (full-text search, GIS, concurrent writes), but requires installation and maintenance. Overkill for single-user desktop unless concurrent access is needed.

context: Content-heavy marketing site with SEO requirements.
expected: SSR: better SEO (search engines get fully-rendered HTML), faster first paint, works without JavaScript. CSR: richer interactivity, smoother page transitions, but slower initial load and poor SEO. For a marketing site, SSR wins — content is static, users expect fast loads, and SEO is critical.
